Standing Order: Standing Order on Servicemembers or Spouses of Servicemembers Seeking Admission to the Maine Bar
entry.content:
STATE OF MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT STANDING ORDER ON SERVICEMEMBERS OR SPOUSES OF SERVICEMEMBERS SEEKING ADMISSION TO THE MAINE BAR
Effective August 3, 2026 Attorneys who are servicemembers or spouses of servicemembers assigned to Maine and who wish to be licensed in Maine while they or their spouses are stationed here may seek waiver of strict compliance with the duration of practice requirement of the rule g overning admission by motion without examination, Maine Bar Admission Rule 11A(a)(2). The Maine Supreme Judicial Court, the Maine Board of Overseers of the Bar, and the Maine Board of Bar Examiners are committed to working with these applicants to accommodate their unique circumstances and to expedite the bar application process to the extent possible when they or their spouses’ service brings them to Maine. The Court will consider requests for waiver on a case -by-case basis, depending on the individual circumstances of the applicant. Servicemembers and spouses of servicemembers are encouraged to contact the Maine Supreme Judicial Court Clerk’s Office at (207)822-4146 for more information about the waiver process. Servicemembers and spouses of servicemembers assigned to Maine who wish to take the Maine bar examination but have missed a deadline to apply for the exam, should also contact the Maine Board of Bar Examiners at (207)623-2464 or execdir@mainebarexaminers.org for assistance. Promulgation Date: 8/3/2026 FOR THE COURT:
/s/ VALERIE STANFILL Chief Justice
Andrew M. Mead Catherine R. Connors Rick E. Lawrence Wayne R. Douglas Julia M. Lipez Christopher C. Taub

entry.title: Standing Order: Standing Order Regarding Admininstrative Order JB-24-03 Pilot Program to Conditionally Authorize Law Student Externs to Provide Public Defense Services
entry.content:
STATE OF MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT STANDING ORDER REGARDING ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER JB-24-03 PILOT PROGRAM TO CONDITIONALLY AUTHORIZE LAW STUDENT EXTERNS TO PROVIDE PUBLIC DEFENSE SERVICES
Effective: September 4, 2026
On December 18, 2024, the Supreme Judicial Court adopted Administrative Order JB-24-03, Pilot Program to Conditionally Authorize Law Student Externs to Provide Public Defense Services. The order provides that it expires on September 5, 2026.
The Court has not determined whether to adopt the program permanently. There are, however, students enrolled in externships for the fall semester of 2026 who will be unable to participate in the externships if the order is allowed to expire.
Because it will take time to determine whether the program will be made permanent, but the Court does not wish to prevent the currently enrolled students from participating in their externships, it is hereby ORDERED that the effective term of the pilot program established by Administrative Order JB-24- 03 is extended through January 15, 2027.
The University of Maine School of Law and the organizations hosting student externs should not arrange for student externs for the spring semester of 2027 without first confirming that the pilot program will remain in effect for that semester.
Dated: September 4, 2026 For the Court:
/s/ Valerie Stanfill Chief Justice
